quote: Our claims experience is losing us customers we spent a fortune to win. I want it fixed, not studied.
Half my team's day is chasing documents that should have come with the claim in the first place.
I sign off every claim, even a ₦150,000 windscreen. I do them on Fridays because the week is full of meetings.
Customers call three or four times a week asking where their claim is. We don't know either without opening five screens.
We drive across Lagos to look at a cracked windscreen. A photo would do. Port Harcourt has only two assessors.
Agents send forms by bus to the branch. Half are missing the police report or the photos. Agents are paid on sales, not claims.
If assessors can approve payments, who checks them? Any change has to keep a second pair of eyes on the money.
The claims system is fifteen years old. I'd rather replace it than patch it, but that's a year's work.
The regulator expects claims settled promptly and complaints answered. Our complaint numbers are starting to be noticed.
I sent my documents twice. Nobody told me what was missing until I called. It took seven weeks.
